cases.scenario: A paid mobile journey opens the scheduler without completing it.
cases.proof: Source fields and the opaque journey key survive the scheduler handoff.

cases.scenario: One controlled production appointment request commits successfully.
cases.proof: One scheduler request ID joins to one downstream row and one primary event.

cases.scenario: The success state is refreshed after a committed appointment request.
cases.proof: The existing request and event IDs are reused and no second event is created.

cases.scenario: The browser returns to the form and repeats the same submission.
cases.proof: The repeated submission resolves to the canonical request dedupe key.

cases.scenario: A webhook or transport process retries a committed request.
cases.proof: Retry delivery reuses the immutable event ID and downstream upsert key.

cases.scenario: A controlled QA submission carries a QA run ID and is_test true.
cases.proof: The record is visible as test evidence but excluded from lead, appointment, booking, and Google outcome totals.

cases.scenario: A form receipt succeeds but the scheduler never commits an appointment request.
cases.proof: No scheduler request ID exists and no primary event is eligible.

cases.scenario: A visitor selects the phone action without a verified conversation or appointment.
cases.proof: The diagnostic click remains secondary and no downstream disposition is inferred.

cases.scenario: Two distinct real appointment requests commit successfully.
cases.proof: Two unique request IDs produce two canonical rows with no shared dedupe key.

cases.scenario: An existing appointment is rescheduled, cancelled, or dispositioned.
cases.proof: The original appointment ID persists and only its status changes.

cases.scenario: A production request arrives without source fields or a usable dedupe key.
cases.proof: The record is quarantined as unresolved and is not force-attributed to Google.

cases.scenario: The same-window summary is rebuilt from source snapshots.
cases.proof: Every count difference has an allowed variance category, evidence reference, and owner role; unknowns remain open.

passConditions: Every case has retained local evidence without raw prospect data.
One eligible real appointment request creates exactly one primary conversion candidate.
Tests, retries, refreshes, repeated submissions, and status changes create no additional primary conversions.
Secondary events remain diagnostic and do not influence the primary appointment count.
The same-window summary and record crosswalk explain every variance or leave it explicitly unresolved.
approvalBoundary: Execution of any live test or configuration change requires exact current approval and before-state capture.
